punchline: Most of us aren't listening to understand. We're just waiting for our turn to reply.
thirty_sec: Stephen Covey tells the story of an eye doctor who hears your complaint, takes off his own glasses and hands them to you, saying they've worked for him for years. You put them on and see worse. That's what most advice is like: prescribed before anyone diagnosed. Covey's fix is Habit 5, seek first to understand, then to be understood. People need to feel understood the way they need air. Only after that can they hear you.
question: Could you explain the other person's side so well that they'd say, 'Yes, that's exactly it'?
